title: “Monks, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon your desire for it. And what, monks, is impermanent? Form, monks, is impermanent … Feeling … Perception ……
content: “Monks, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon your desire for it. And what, monks, is impermanent? Form, monks, is impermanent … Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is impermanent — there you should abandon your desire. Whatever is impermanent, monks, there you should abandon your desire.”

title: Elder Sivaka: Impermanent are these houses, Built again and again. Seeking the house-builder, Birth is suffering. O house-builder, you are seen! From now on, you…
content:
Elder Sivaka:

Impermanent are these houses,
Built again and again.
Seeking the house-builder,
Birth is suffering.

O house-builder, you are seen!
From now on, you cannot
Build a house again.
All your rafters are broken,
The ridge-pole is shattered.
The mind has been pushed from the stream,
Here, it is destroyed.

title: “Monks, when a monk has abandoned ignorance and aroused true knowledge, then with the abandonment of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge, he does…
content: “Monks, when a monk has abandoned ignorance and aroused true knowledge, then with the abandonment of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge, he does not form any volitional formation, does not generate any kamma. Without forming, without generating, he does not cling to anything in the world. Without clinging, he is not agitated. Without agitation, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “Here, venerable sir, a person has a stain and he truly knows: ‘There is a stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be…
content: “Here, venerable sir, a person has a stain and he truly knows: ‘There is a stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will arouse desire, make effort, arouse energy to abandon that stain. He will die without greed, without ill-will, without delusion, without stain, his mind unpolluted.’ Venerable sir, just as a bronze bowl brought from the market or from the smithy, covered with dust and grime, and the owner uses it, wipes it, and does not throw it into a dusty place – that bowl, after a time, becomes more purified and cleaner.”

title: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs,…
content: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs, or by jackals, or by various worms. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

title: Māra: You will not escape, You will not escape this world. What use is this practice of seclusion to you? Enjoy sensual pleasures — Do…
content:
Māra:

You will not escape,
You will not escape this world.
What use is this practice of seclusion to you?
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
Do not have regrets later.

Elder Nun Selā:

Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears —
They cut the aggregates to pieces.
What you call the pleasure of life —
For me, that sensual pleasure
Is no longer enticing.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed.
The mass of darkness,
The blinding darkness, has been shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are Māra,
You are defeated.

title: “Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted…
content: “Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … with feeling … with perception … with formations … with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, knowledge arises: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not…
content:
“Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Would that man drink from that bronze cup if he knew: ‘If I drink from this, I will meet death or deadly suffering’?”
“No, venerable sir.”
“So too, Sunakkhatta, a monk should surely guard himself in regard to the six sense-bases. Knowing that ‘Attachment is the root of suffering,’ he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. It does not happen that he would still focus his body on attachment or direct his mind to attachment.”

title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
content: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

title: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?”…
content: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?” - “The sign of the beautiful.” For one who attends unwisely to the sign of the beautiful, unarisen greed arises and arisen greed increases and grows. This, good sirs, is the cause, this is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed and for the growth and increase of arisen greed.
